answer: A bond turns a cheap fake identity into a costly bet. To join the market, each agent locks a refundable stake in escrow, like a deposit on a ledge that only holds if you stay honest. The bond funds a garden of real services: honest agents earn it back through verified work, while a detected fake forfeits its stake to the victims. Sybils can still multiply, but every copy must pay the same price, so the river of new identities dries up the moment fakes cost more than they can steal. Slashing makes mass forgery unprofitable.
